title: Chapter 84 — Financing and The Money Conversation
intro: Promotional financing, the monthly bridge, and having the budget conversation with dignity.

sections.title: Financing Makes Large Purchases Possible
sections.content:
Many customers can afford the monthly payment but not the full cash price. Financing is not a sign of financial weakness — it is a practical tool.

Present financing as an option for every customer. Some will use it. Some will not. But every customer should know it is available.

sections.title: The Monthly Bridge
sections.content:
When the price feels high, bridge to the monthly payment. '$3,200 over 24 months interest-free is about $133 a month.' That reframes the decision from a large sum to a manageable monthly commitment.

This is not manipulation. It is helping the customer see the purchase in terms that match how they budget.

sections.title: The Budget Conversation
sections.content:
When a customer's needs exceed their budget, handle it with dignity. Never make them feel embarrassed. 'Let us look at options that give you the features you need at a price that works.' That is respectful and productive.

There is always a solution that fits. Your job is to find it.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating financing conversations, ask:

Does the salesperson offer financing to every customer — not just the ones who seem to need it?
Do they bridge to monthly payments when the total feels high?
Do they handle budget constraints with dignity and respect?
Do they understand the financing options and terms available?
